subject: RE: HealthSync telemetry export carveout — product/security sign-off needed
messages:
From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@healthsync.com>

Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data processing addendum — telemetry export carveout request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the inference latency looked great. Legal at HealthSync has a few outstanding concerns before we finalize the DPA. We've attached our proposed redline (HealthSync_DPA_redline_20280719.pdf). The main ask: allow telemetry export to our analytics vendor (MixSight) for product usage and billing metrics. We limited the scope to aggregated metrics and excluded any raw KV cache snapshots or PII, and we've proposed a 90-day retention window.

Quick summary of the carveout clauses we inserted:
- Telemetry exports allowed to named analytics subprocessor (MixSight) for billing/usage only
- Retention for exported telemetry: 90 days
- No training of models on HealthSync customer data

Can Redwood confirm whether this is acceptable and what operational controls you'd need (pseudonymization, contract with MixSight, audit rights, etc.)? We need a DPA counter-signature by Jul 26 to stay on our Q3 roadmap.

Appreciate a quick triage.

Cheers,
Emily Rogers
Head of Procurement, HealthSync Labs

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data processing addendum — telemetry export carveout request

Vanessa — thanks for the ping and the redline. Quick legal take after an initial pass (attached annotated PDF):

- We can accept telemetry exports to a named analytics subprocessor provided:
  * Redwood requires a written Subprocessor Addendum between HealthSync and MixSight that mirrors our security controls (encryption in transit/at rest, access controls).
  * Export payload must be limited to aggregated, pseudonymized metrics; no raw KV cache, no identifiers that allow re-identification.
  * Audit clause: Redwood retains the right to audit exports on a quarterly cadence for 12 months after export to confirm pseudonymization and scope.

- Retention: 90 days is acceptable ONLY if combined with strong pseudonymization and a formal retention schedule. Prefer recommending 60 days but can make 90 conditional on the Subprocessor Addendum.

- No-training clause: we should explicitly prohibit model training on HealthSync customer data in the DPA; add an express carveout that prevents downstream training by MixSight or any downstream vendor.

- Additional asks: data flow diagram (simple link) and confirmation that exported telemetry excludes request/response payloads and KV cache snapshots.

I'll attach an annotated PDF with specific clause edits. If product/security can confirm technical mitigations, legal can prepare a counter-redline to send back.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachments: HealthSync_DPA_redline_20280719_annotated.pdf
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data processing addendum — telemetry export carveout request

Thanks — operational notes from product/security: 

- Risk surface: current runtime telemetry includes both aggregated metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) and internal debugging snapshots (KV cache traces, request IDs). We cannot export internal debugging snapshots as part of a customer-facing telemetry export.
- Implementation plan to comply with the carveout:
  1) Add an export filter that only emits aggregated metrics (per-route token counts, latency p95/p50, error category counts).
  2) Strip or hash any request identifiers; remove KV cache contents entirely from export.
  3) Add a flag in the Export Service to enforce a retention TTL (default 60 days). We can allow 90 days only if legal requires and MixSight signs Subproc Addendum.
  4) Product will ship a config toggle and a short runbook; security will require periodic verification of pseudonymization.

- Contingency: If HealthSync insists on raw exports, we will not accept — that's a hard no.

Ben Carter
Principal Product Manager, Runtime & Security | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Data processing addendum — telemetry export carveout request

Emily — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Internal quick summary and proposed path forward: 

What Redwood can accept today (pending documents and a short tech change):
- Export to named analytics vendor (MixSight) limited to aggregated, pseudonymized metrics only (no KV cache, no request/response payloads).
- Retention: default 60 days in Redwood's export pipeline. We can agree to 90 days if HealthSync and MixSight execute a Subprocessor Addendum that includes the security controls Olga listed and allows Redwood quarterly verification for 12 months post-export.
- Explicit no-training clause: Redwood will add language preventing MixSight from using exported telemetry for model training on HealthSync customer data.

Next steps / timeline:
- HealthSync / MixSight to provide a copy of the Subprocessor Addendum for legal review (due Jul 22).
- Legal (Olga) to prepare a counter-redline that includes the Subprocessor Addendum requirement and audit right (target by Jul 22).
- Product/Security (Ben) to ship the export filter + TTL toggle to staging (target Jul 29).
- Vanessa to coordinate a short sync on Jul 25 to finalize DPA language and confirm the export flow (30 min).

If that timeline works, I'll package Redwood's counter-redline and return it for HealthSync review.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
